title: 2017 AMC 12B 19
statement: Let \(N = 123456789101112\ldots4344\) be the \(79\)-digit number that is formed by writing the integers from \(1\) to \(44\) in order, one after the other. What is the remainder when \(N\) is divided by \(45?\)

solutions.text:
The last digit of \(N\) is \(4,\) so \(N \equiv 4 \pmod 5.\) For mod \(9,\) sum the digits: the numbers \(1\)–\(9\) contribute their digits, the tens digits of \(10\)–\(44\) and the units digits together sum to \(270,\) which is a multiple of \(9,\) so \(N \equiv 0 \pmod 9.\) The number \(N - 9\) is then a multiple of \(9,\) and its last digit is \(5,\) so it is a multiple of \(5;\) hence \(N - 9\) is a multiple of \(45.\) Therefore \(N \equiv 9 \pmod{45}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Since \(45 = 9 \cdot 5,\) find \(N \bmod 5\) (the last digit) and \(N \bmod 9\) (the digit sum)
The digit sum is a multiple of \(9,\) so \(N \equiv 0 \pmod 9;\) combine with the residue mod \(5\)
